reviews.review: Chat, we misjudged this game. It was actually not that bad, the criticism was harsh true, but that does not necessitate that the vidja ain't worth playing. Sometimes it's okay to play games that aren't ya know game of the year. Sometimes we like playing games that aren't stellar. IT's okay it happens ya know. We can't always get amazing games all the time as is evident with this game. But does that mean we cannot enjoy this game? NO I Say, We can if we choose to. Enjoy it in our own ways.
Incredible gameplay.  Love the freedom with skills, jump jets and the Nomad.  Love how the Nomad doesn't blow up when you go over a small cliff. Great graphics!

This game feels like it received a giant budget, hired a lot of people to work on it and then halfway through decided to publish it as finished product. NPCs teleporting while talking to them, textures on highest settings look worse than ME2, music is ok.

Combat in this game was the easiest out of all mass effect games, not only because you can change your skillset whenever you want, but also because enemies had tracking issues and were just often standing around aimlessly. But back to skillset, I still don't understand why can we only use 3 abilities? Massive downgrade when it's compared to trilogy. 

Next issue: The story
Reskinned trilogy with the best parts cut out trying to make it's own legacy, but devs forgot to actually put something interesting in there to attract players. Story was extremely shallow, you could guess everything that is gonna happen. The second you notice that kett are reskinned reapers (or collectors even to be exact), you just know 3 next steps in story.

Talking with companions was weird at best. You talk to someone, go through all options, they don't want to talk anymore, land on planet, go back to ship, new options to go through. Same problem with NPCs, talk to someone on Nexus, go back to ship, instantly there's an email to meet them again. It's just artificially extending the game by providing nothing at all.

Research and development is the most useless mechanic in this game. You don't get enough points to reliably be on top of all upgrades, so you have to choose, often when you reach a milestone level you can't get the whole set of armour or all the weapons you're using. But you can just go to a store and buy all these weapons the second you reach that level. So a thing I have to research is just a common good on the nexus and I can buy it for a fraction of the price it would cost me if I had to buy the materials. 

There's also the small details like ark hyperion still being on tram screen in Nexus and other stuff like this, but seeing how they didn't care to fix even the big things, I'm not gonna waste more time on it.
In total it took me 3 attempts to finish this game, 1st time I dropped it after around 2h, because it was messy at start. 2nd run was the same, but I lasted until Voeld, nothing changed in terms of bugs, the combat just exhausted me so I stopped playing. This time I played this game before trilogy to motivate myself that I'll play it after finishing it and so I did. Tried going for 100%, but then my game crashed after ~30h, it seemed fine so I continued but my save was somehow changed, realized it when it was too late, but my romance was reset and also Drack's loyalty mission was gone, so wasn't possible for me to finish it, while he was one of my two squadmates, so I just rushed the Meridian to be done with it.

Overall 2/10 game, would be 3 but I hated Mako and this game had more of it. Let's hope they learned their lesson with next game in production. Don't buy it unless it's on a 95% discount and you just happen to have absolutely nothing to do, not even watch paint dry or grass grow.
